4jv3ba.q: It is forbidden to drive a motor vehicle on public roads without the driving licence required for that type of vehicle.
4jv3ba.why: You need the licence (patente) of the right category for the vehicle you drive; driving without it is prohibited and penalised.

p4brwq.q: As a rule, it is forbidden to drive an unregistered motor vehicle on public roads.
p4brwq.why: A vehicle may only circulate once it is registered (immatricolato), with plates and a registration document (carta di circolazione).

d8ou9u.q: It is forbidden to use a motor vehicle on public roads when you do not have the road tax payment receipt with you.
d8ou9u.why: You do not have to carry the road tax (bollo) receipt while driving; it is not a document required on board.

iu003k.q: It is forbidden to drive on public roads a motor vehicle fitted with a trial plate (targa prova).
iu003k.why: A trial plate (targa prova) legally allows vehicles to circulate on public roads for testing or demonstration under authorisation.

3ot15d.q: It is forbidden to use a motor vehicle on public roads when the registration document is in the name of someone other than the driver.
3ot15d.why: You may drive a vehicle owned by someone else; the registration document (carta di circolazione) need not be in the driver's name.

1ypoymi.q: On public roads it is forbidden to use a motor vehicle if its warranty has expired.
1ypoymi.why: A manufacturer or dealer warranty is a commercial matter and does not affect legal use. Valid third-party insurance (RC auto) is what is required.

152mawx.q: It is forbidden to use a motor vehicle on public roads when you do not have the certificate of ownership with you.
152mawx.why: The certificate of ownership (certificato di proprietà) need not be carried in the vehicle; the licence and registration document are what you must have.

7alffo.q: To be allowed to circulate, a motor vehicle must be fitted with identification plates so that the owner of the vehicle can be traced.
7alffo.why: Plates (targhe) identify the vehicle and let authorities trace its owner; a vehicle cannot circulate without them.

ksikxq.q: To be allowed to circulate, a motor vehicle must carry its registration document (carta di circolazione).
ksikxq.why: The carta di circolazione is the vehicle's identity document and must always be on board.

1ajkz5u.q: To be allowed to circulate, a motor vehicle must be equipped with the mobile warning triangle.
1ajkz5u.why: The warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) is mandatory equipment on cars, used when stopped by a breakdown or accident.

tccdzu.q: To be allowed to circulate, a car must have a "kasko" (comprehensive) insurance policy.
tccdzu.why: Only third-party liability insurance (RC auto) is compulsory; kasko, which covers your own vehicle, is optional.

150h9ee.q: Vehicle plates must be firmly fixed and correctly positioned.
150h9ee.why: Plates (targhe) must be securely attached in the position designated on the vehicle.

1h5vmfv.q: Vehicle plates must always be clearly legible.
1h5vmfv.why: Plates must be legible at all times so the vehicle can always be identified.

q2s1vr.q: Vehicle plates must not be dirty.
q2s1vr.why: A dirty plate may become unreadable, so it must be kept clean.

4lpwpt.q: Vehicle plates must not be tampered with or counterfeited.
4lpwpt.why: Altering or forging plates is prohibited and punishable, including under criminal law.

1kvi5jd.q: Motor vehicles used for driving practice must be fitted, both at the front and at the rear, with retroreflective panels bearing the letter "P" (principiante, beginner).
1kvi5jd.why: A car used for driving practice must show retroreflective panels with the letter P (principiante) on the front and the rear.

c8mkb2.q: Vehicle plates may be bent to fit their mounting better.
c8mkb2.why: Plates must not be bent or altered; they must stay intact and legible.

1ppby8a.q: With an AM licence you may drive light quadricycles.
1ppby8a.why: The AM licence covers two- and three-wheeled mopeds and light quadricycles (quadricicli leggeri).

12no8vf.q: With an AM licence you may drive two-wheeled mopeds.
12no8vf.why: The AM licence covers two-wheeled mopeds (ciclomotori).

pi43pw.q: With an AM licence you may drive three-wheeled mopeds.
pi43pw.why: The AM licence also covers three-wheeled mopeds.

9wypfg.q: The AM licence can be obtained at 14 years of age.
9wypfg.why: The minimum age for the AM licence is 14.

1it4keh.q: The AM licence entitles you to drive mopeds with a combustion engine of no more than 50 cm3.
1it4keh.why: AM covers mopeds with a combustion engine up to 50 cm3.

1dkr0dm.q: The AM licence allows holders aged 14 or over to drive mopeds in all European Union countries.
1dkr0dm.why: At 14 the AM licence is valid in Italy; in other EU countries it is generally valid only from age 16.

1oofk6q.q: With an AM licence you may drive non-light quadricycles with power up to 7 kW.
1oofk6q.why: AM covers light quadricycles only; non-light quadricycles require at least a B1 licence.

4ljo4n.q: The AM licence entitles you to drive motorcycles, provided they have an electric motor.
4ljo4n.why: AM does not cover motorcycles, even electric ones; you need at least an A1 licence.

1cy7ej1.q: The AM licence can be issued without taking theory and practical exams, provided the applicant is of legal age.
1cy7ej1.why: Adults too must pass the theory and practical tests to obtain an AM licence.

o1mp39.q: An AM licence held for at least 3 years entitles you to drive motorcycles up to 11 kW.
o1mp39.why: Holding AM longer does not extend it; to ride motorcycles you need an A1 licence or higher.

t45lqa.q: With an A1 licence you may drive motorcycles (with or without sidecar) up to 125 cm3, with power not exceeding 11 kW and a power/weight ratio not exceeding 0.1 kW/kg.
t45lqa.why: These are the A1 limits: 125 cm3, 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg.

4t0i6r.q: With an A1 licence you may drive motor tricycles with power not exceeding 15 kW.
4t0i6r.why: A1 covers motor tricycles up to 15 kW.

h1d6n5.q: With an A1 licence you may drive agricultural machines that fall within the size and mass limits set for motorcycles.
h1d6n5.why: A1 includes agricultural machines within the size and mass limits for motorcycles.

1x5r8qy.q: The A1 licence can be obtained by those who are at least 16 years old.
1x5r8qy.why: The minimum age for an A1 licence is 16.

rzycxi.q: The A1 licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the AM licence.
rzycxi.why: Higher categories include lower ones, so A1 also covers everything AM allows.

1m2mir6.q: The A1 licence can only be obtained by those who already hold the AM licence.
1m2mir6.why: A1 can be obtained directly at 16; holding AM first is not required.

1u6qbtc.q: The A1 licence entitles you to drive all motorcycles with an engine capacity of up to 125 cm3.
1u6qbtc.why: Besides 125 cm3, power must not exceed 11 kW and 0.1 kW/kg, so a more powerful 125 cm3 bike is excluded.

1nh9s17.q: With an A1 licence you may drive tricycles of more than 15 kW, but only if the driver is of legal age.
1nh9s17.why: With A1 the 15 kW tricycle limit applies at any age; above that you need an A licence.

441ihm.q: With an A1 licence you may drive non-exceptional working machines (macchine operatrici).
441ihm.why: A1 does not cover working machines (macchine operatrici), only agricultural machines within motorcycle limits.

lzv3vn.q: The A1 licence allows a driver under 18 to carry a passenger, but only if the passenger is of legal age.
lzv3vn.why: Carrying a passenger depends on the vehicle having a passenger seat on its registration document, not on the passenger's age.

i2vipc.q: After the first two years from obtaining it, the A1 licence automatically becomes an A2 licence and, after a further two years, becomes an A licence entitling you to drive any motorcycle.
i2vipc.why: Licences never upgrade automatically with time; moving to A2 or A requires the proper procedure, including a practical test.

akqkk4.q: With an A2 licence you may drive motorcycles (with or without sidecar) up to 35 kW, with a power/weight ratio not exceeding 0.2 kW/kg, provided they are not derived from a version of the same model developing more than double the maximum power.
akqkk4.why: These are the A2 limits: 35 kW, 0.2 kW/kg and not derived from a version with more than double the power.

13ijri8.q: The A2 licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1 and AM licences.
13ijri8.why: A2 includes the lower categories, A1 and AM.

d5f3k5.q: The A2 licence can be obtained by those who are at least 18 years old.
d5f3k5.why: The minimum age for an A2 licence is 18.

16rc7ty.q: The A2 licence allows the holder to carry a passenger only if a passenger seat is provided on the vehicle's registration document.
16rc7ty.why: A passenger may be carried only if the registration document (carta di circolazione) provides a passenger seat.

z0c66l.q: A holder of an A2 licence for at least two years may obtain the A licence, which entitles them to drive all motorcycles, even if under 24.
z0c66l.why: After 2 years with A2 you can step up to A by gradual access, from age 20, with a practical test.

1g83tg.q: A holder of an A2 licence may also drive agricultural machines that fall within the size and mass limits of motorcycles.
1g83tg.why: A2 also covers agricultural machines within the size and mass limits of motorcycles.

ng2amy.q: The A2 licence can be obtained by those who are at least 20 years old.
ng2amy.why: The minimum age for A2 is 18, not 20; 20 is the age for gradual access to category A.

fq8085.q: With an A2 licence you may drive motorcycles (with or without sidecar) up to 25 kW, with a power/weight ratio not exceeding 0.2 kW/kg, provided they are not derived from a version developing more than triple the maximum power.
fq8085.why: The A2 limit is 35 kW, and the original version must not exceed double the power, not triple.

kvo2y.q: A holder of an A2 licence for at least two years may obtain the A licence entitling them to drive all motorcycles only if they already hold the AM licence and are over 24.
kvo2y.why: Gradual access to A requires 2 years of A2 and age 20; holding AM and being over 24 are irrelevant.

1xrs3h.q: A holder of an A2 licence may not drive motorcycles of more than 150 cm3 and more than 25 kW.
1xrs3h.why: A2 is limited by power (35 kW) and power/weight ratio, not by 150 cm3 or 25 kW.

12chl3s.q: The A2 licence can only be obtained if you already hold the A1 licence.
12chl3s.why: A2 can be obtained directly at 18 without holding A1 first.

11vkjt0.q: The A2 licence only allows driving mopeds and light quadricycles.
11vkjt0.why: A2 covers motorcycles up to 35 kW and includes the lower categories too.

7z02tt.q: The A2 licence does not allow driving any type of motor tricycle.
7z02tt.why: A2 allows motor tricycles up to 15 kW, as A1 does.

171s0xn.q: With an A licence you may drive all motorcycles (with or without sidecar).
171s0xn.why: The A licence covers all motorcycles with no limit on engine size or power.

pvts3s.q: With an A licence you may drive all motor tricycles, but only if the driver is at least 21 years old.
pvts3s.why: Tricycles over 15 kW require an A licence and a minimum age of 21.

gjcdpm.q: The A licence entitles you to drive motorcycles over 50 cm3 even if they exceed 45 km/h.
gjcdpm.why: Vehicles over 50 cm3 or 45 km/h are motorcycles, not mopeds, and A covers them.

s5stri.q: The A licence can be obtained with direct access, by those who have not held an A2 licence for at least 2 years, only if they are at least 24.
s5stri.why: Direct access to A, without 2 years of A2, requires being at least 24.

my31jk.q: The A licence can be obtained at 20 years of age, by gradual access, by those who have held an A2 licence for at least 2 years.
my31jk.why: Gradual access to A requires age 20 and at least 2 years holding an A2 licence.

pk2upb.q: The A licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1, A2 and AM licences.
pk2upb.why: A includes all the lower categories: A2, A1 and AM.

1tmu37d.q: With an A licence you may also drive tricycles of more than 15 kW, but only if the driver is at least 21 years old.
1tmu37d.why: Above 15 kW, tricycles require an A licence and age 21 or over.

1pgniwh.q: With an A licence you may drive motorcycles (with or without sidecar) of any engine capacity, provided their power is below 35 kW for the first 2 years after obtaining it.
1pgniwh.why: The A licence has no power limit, not even in the first years after obtaining it.

1bw8x58.q: With an A licence you may drive non-light quadricycles, whatever the driver's age.
1bw8x58.why: Non-light quadricycles are not covered by A; they need a B1 or B licence.

3flzy4.q: The A licence can be obtained by gradual access at 18 years of age by those who have held an A1 licence for at least 2 years.
3flzy4.why: Gradual access to A starts at age 20 and requires 2 years of A2, not A1.

1315z04.q: With an A licence you may also drive tricycles of more than 15 kW, whatever the driver's age.
1315z04.why: Tricycles above 15 kW require a minimum age of 21.

147xjw2.q: The A licence can be obtained with direct access, even by those who have not held an A2 licence for at least 2 years, provided they are at least 21.
147xjw2.why: Direct access requires age 24, not 21; 21 is only the age for tricycles above 15 kW.

u0qhnj.q: An A licence obtained by direct access at 24 or over allows you to drive all motorcycles but only in Italy; to drive abroad a further exam is necessary.
u0qhnj.why: The A licence is also valid abroad (in the EU) with no further exam.

1kpq709.q: To obtain the A licence you must in any case be at least 24 years old.
1kpq709.why: 24 is required only for direct access; with 2 years of A2 you can get A at 20.

10o4so0.q: The B1 licence can be obtained at 16 years of age.
10o4so0.why: The minimum age for a B1 licence is 16.

ap1usi.q: The B1 licence entitles you to drive some types of non-light quadricycles.
ap1usi.why: B1 covers certain non-light quadricycles, within the category limits.

179rtfb.q: The B1 licence entitles you to drive non-light quadricycles with handlebars (quads).
179rtfb.why: Handlebar quads are among the non-light quadricycles covered by B1.

1o38y0c.q: The B1 licence entitles you to drive motorcycles (with or without sidecar) up to 125 cm3, with power not exceeding 11 kW and a power/weight ratio not exceeding 0.1 kW/kg.
1o38y0c.why: Motorcycles of that type belong to category A1; B1 covers non-light quadricycles.

dhlb29.q: With a B1 licence you may drive all motor tricycles, but only if the driver is already 18 years old.
dhlb29.why: B1 does not cover all motor tricycles; it is the category for non-light quadricycles.

nulsd.q: The B1 licence entitles you to drive single-seat cars, or cars with at most three seats including the driver, provided you travel without passengers on board.
nulsd.why: B1 does not cover cars; you need a B licence to drive them.

gb0jyv.q: The B1 licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1 licence.
gb0jyv.why: B1 does not include A1; they are separate categories, B1 for quadricycles and A1 for motorcycles.

1ej46do.q: A holder of a B1 licence who wants to obtain the B licence will only have to take an additional theory exam.
1ej46do.why: Moving from B1 to B is not just an extra theory exam; the exams required for B must be taken.

sj7f4r.q: The B licence entitles you to drive motor vehicles with a maximum authorised mass of no more than 3.5 tonnes, designed to carry no more than eight persons in addition to the driver.
sj7f4r.why: Licence B covers motor vehicles up to 3.5 t maximum authorised mass with at most eight passengers plus the driver.

11e06at.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive cars, even when towing a light trailer (mass up to 750 kg).
11e06at.why: Category B covers cars, and you may tow a light trailer of up to 750 kg without extra qualifications.

4mm696.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive motorhomes (autocaravan) with a maximum authorised mass not exceeding 3.5 tonnes.
4mm696.why: Category B covers any motor vehicle up to 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass, including motorhomes (autocaravan) within that limit.

ezpt7p.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive agricultural machines, including those classed as exceptional.
ezpt7p.why: Category B covers all agricultural machines (macchine agricole), including the ones classed as exceptional (eccezionali).

1mq24nf.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive cars towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kg), provided the maximum authorised mass of the combination does not exceed 3.5 tonnes.
1mq24nf.why: With category B you may tow a trailer over 750 kg as long as the whole combination stays within 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass.

lmkcg3.q: Category B licence allows you to drive, but only within Italy, the vehicles that can be driven with an A1 licence.
lmkcg3.why: Category B lets you ride A1 vehicles (light motorcycles), but this entitlement is valid only in Italy.

z2r3hg.q: Category B licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with AM and B1 licences.
z2r3hg.why: Category B automatically includes the lower categories AM (mopeds) and B1 (light quadricycles).

1do3iwg.q: Category B licence allows you to drive, only within Italy and if the driver is at least 21, motor tricycles with power exceeding 15 kW.
1do3iwg.why: In Italy, category B holders aged 21 or over may drive motor tricycles above 15 kW; the entitlement is not valid abroad.

kp6xbt.q: Category B licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with A2 and A licences.
kp6xbt.why: Category B does not cover A2 or A motorcycles. Those need their own licence, obtained with a separate test.

mqezaa.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive buses designed to carry up to 16 seats, excluding the driver.
mqezaa.why: Category B does not cover buses. Even a minibus with 16 passenger seats needs category D1.

kj7jgb.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive lorries with a maximum authorised mass above 3.5 tonnes but not above 7.5 tonnes.
kj7jgb.why: Category B stops at 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass. Lorries between 3.5 and 7.5 tonnes need category C1.

174irg7.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive exceptional operating machines (macchine operatrici eccezionali).
174irg7.why: Category B covers exceptional agricultural machines, but not exceptional operating machines (macchine operatrici eccezionali), which need a higher category.

p7vapm.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive only cars with at most 9 seats including the driver.
p7vapm.why: Category B is not limited to cars. It also covers quadricycles, agricultural machines and other vehicles up to 3,500 kg.

o81v8q.q: Category B licence entitles you to drive cars even when they tow trailers with a mass above 3,500 kg.
o81v8q.why: Category B does not allow towing a trailer heavier than 3,500 kg. That requires a higher licence such as BE.

1n0lpyb.q: Category B licence allows you to drive a car towing a trailer, with the combination having a mass of 4,500 kg.
1n0lpyb.why: Plain category B limits the combination to 3,500 kg (4,250 kg with code 96). A 4,500 kg combination needs category BE.

1mp14tr.q: Category B licence obtained after the age of 24 entitles you to drive all motorcycles.
1mp14tr.why: Category B never covers motorcycles in general, whatever your age. You need an A1, A2 or A licence.

d23ys.q: Category B licence allows you to drive all motorhomes (autocaravan).
d23ys.why: Category B covers only motorhomes up to 3,500 kg. Heavier ones need a higher category such as C1.

7q479x.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 allows you to drive cars towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kg), provided the maximum authorised mass of the combination does not exceed 4,250 kg.
7q479x.why: Code 96 on a category B licence extends towing to non-light trailers, with a combination limit of 4,250 kg.

5v1mdw.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 can also be obtained after getting category B, by passing a driving test on a specific vehicle.
5v1mdw.why: You can add code 96 to an existing B licence later by passing a practical test with a suitable combination of vehicle and trailer.

52mz2n.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 can also be obtained at the same time as category B, by taking a driving test on a specific vehicle.
52mz2n.why: Code 96 can be earned together with category B by taking the extra driving test on a specific vehicle combination.

1i9vaud.q: Harmonised code 96, shown on a category B licence, entitles you to drive motor vehicles towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kg), provided the maximum authorised mass of the combination does not exceed 4,250 kg.
1i9vaud.why: Code 96 allows a category B holder to tow a trailer over 750 kg when the whole combination does not exceed 4,250 kg.

1b9mmj7.q: To drive a car towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kg) with a combination mass above 3,500 kg but not above 4,250 kg, a category B licence with harmonised code 96 is enough.
1b9mmj7.why: For combinations between 3,500 and 4,250 kg with a heavy trailer, category B plus code 96 is sufficient; category BE is not needed.

1qdw4o3.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 entitles you to drive articulated vehicles (autosnodati) with a maximum authorised mass above 4,250 kg but not above 7,500 kg.
1qdw4o3.why: Code 96 only extends towing to combinations up to 4,250 kg. It gives no entitlement for heavier articulated vehicles (autosnodati).

figzjw.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 entitles you to drive motorcycles with power up to 35 kW.
figzjw.why: Code 96 concerns only towing a trailer. It gives no motorcycle entitlement; for up to 35 kW you need category A2.

14hn13i.q: Category B licence with harmonised code 96 can be obtained only if you already hold an A licence.
14hn13i.why: Code 96 depends on holding category B only. Having an A licence is not a requirement.

153hxsr.q: Harmonised code 96, shown on a category B licence, entitles you to drive motor vehicles towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kg), with a combination mass above 4,250 kg but not above 6,000 kg.
153hxsr.why: The code 96 limit is 4,250 kg for the whole combination. Above that you need category BE.

1k1mznc.q: Harmonised code 96, shown on a category B licence, means the holder can drive a car towing a trailer only in Italy.
1k1mznc.why: Code 96 is an EU harmonised code, so it is valid in other EU countries too, not just in Italy.

zu629t.q: Category BE licence entitles you to drive combinations made up of a motor vehicle with a maximum authorised mass up to 3,500 kg and a trailer with a mass up to 3,500 kg, even if the combination exceeds 4,250 kg.
zu629t.why: Category BE allows a 3,500 kg vehicle with a trailer of up to 3,500 kg, so the total can be well above 4,250 kg.

1ajc6w1.q: To drive a car towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of 2,000 kg and a combination mass of 4,500 kg, you must hold a category BE licence.
1ajc6w1.why: At 4,500 kg the combination exceeds the 4,250 kg limit of code 96, so category BE is required.

1s4jaig.q: Category BE licence entitles you to drive road trains (autotreni) made up of a motor vehicle with a maximum authorised mass up to 3,500 kg and a trailer with a mass up to 3,500 kg.
1s4jaig.why: Category BE covers a vehicle of up to 3,500 kg towing a trailer of up to 3,500 kg.

1awmuhv.q: Category BE licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with categories AM, B1, B and B with harmonised code 96.
1awmuhv.why: Category BE includes the lower categories AM, B1, B and B with code 96.

84bn8n.q: To drive a motor vehicle with a maximum authorised mass of 3,500 kg towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of 1,000 kg, you must hold a category BE licence.
84bn8n.why: The trailer is over 750 kg and the combination reaches 4,500 kg, above the 3,500 kg limit of plain B, so BE is needed (code 96 only goes to 4,250 kg).

c5j1ej.q: To drive a motor vehicle with a maximum authorised mass of 4,000 kg towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of 2,000 kg, a category BE licence is enough.
c5j1ej.why: The BE category requires the towing vehicle to be within 3,500 kg. A 4,000 kg vehicle needs category C1 (or C1E with trailer).

i7jmg4.q: Category BE licence entitles you to drive combinations made up of a minibus towing a trailer with a mass up to 1,500 kg.
i7jmg4.why: A minibus needs category D1 or D1E. Category BE covers only vehicles up to 3,500 kg carrying at most 8 passengers.

1uh0rrh.q: Category BE licence also entitles you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with categories A, B and C1.
1uh0rrh.why: Category BE does not include A (motorcycles) or C1 (lorries). Those are separate licences.

1jx394b.q: Category BE licence entitles you to drive road trains (autotreni) made up of a motor vehicle with a maximum authorised mass up to 3,500 kg towing a trailer with a mass above 3,500 kg.
1jx394b.why: Category BE allows trailers up to 3,500 kg only. A heavier trailer needs a higher category.

1l32w0.q: Category BE licence can also be obtained at the same time as category B, by taking the driving test on a specific vehicle, but you must be at least 21.
1l32w0.why: Category BE has no minimum age of 21. It is available to B holders, who must pass a practical test on a specific vehicle.

gb8jwi.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, following an offence that carries suspension of the licence as an accessory penalty.
gb8jwi.why: On-the-spot withdrawal (ritiro) applies to violations whose accessory penalty is licence suspension.

1eww8a0.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when it is found that the driver is using a licence that has expired.
1eww8a0.why: Driving with an expired licence leads to immediate withdrawal (ritiro) of the licence.

1xoxhz1.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver is found driving under the influence of alcohol.
1xoxhz1.why: Drink driving (stato di ebbrezza) leads to immediate withdrawal of the licence by the police.

lpdx0a.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, if the driver fails to properly secure a badly arranged load after being told to by the police.
lpdx0a.why: If you do not fix a badly arranged load after the police tell you to, your licence is withdrawn on the spot.

1blz4k5.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, if an accident results in injuries to people.
1blz4k5.why: An accident causing injuries leads to immediate withdrawal of the licence.

1gk1thg.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver, obliged to take a revision exam, has not taken it within the required time.
1gk1thg.why: Failing to take a required revision exam (revisione) within the deadline results in immediate withdrawal of the licence.

1u8s7k9.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver is carrying a passenger who is intoxicated.
1u8s7k9.why: Withdrawal applies only if the driver is drunk. A drunk passenger does not affect the driver's licence.

zn863x.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver drives in Italy with a licence issued by a foreign state in which they are resident.
zn863x.why: A valid licence issued by the driver's foreign country of residence is accepted in Italy, so it is not withdrawn.

lr9eej.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, if the vehicle is driven with tyres of different sizes from those shown in the registration document.
lr9eej.why: Wrong tyre sizes result in a fine, not withdrawal of the licence.

1isbnuz.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, every time the driver commits an offence that results in points being deducted from the licence.
1isbnuz.why: Losing points does not by itself cause withdrawal. Withdrawal applies only to specific serious violations.

1n2hasc.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver drives without having the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) on them.
1n2hasc.why: Not carrying the registration document (carta di circolazione) results in a fine, not withdrawal of the licence.

u9usr.q: The driving licence is withdrawn immediately, while driving, when the driver drives without the vehicle's certificate of ownership on them.
u9usr.why: The certificate of ownership does not have to be carried in the vehicle, and its absence never leads to licence withdrawal.

gzsimk.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when doubts arise that the driver still meets the required physical and mental requirements.
gzsimk.why: A licence revision (revisione) can be ordered if there are doubts about the driver's continuing physical and mental fitness.

181lk8p.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered by the Motor Vehicle Office (Motorizzazione civile) or by the Prefect.
181lk8p.why: A licence revision can be ordered by the Motorizzazione civile or by the Prefect (Prefetto).

1fi53yz.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered following a road accident that caused serious injuries to people.
1fi53yz.why: A road accident causing serious injuries can lead to an order for licence revision.

7n8v50.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when doubts arise that the driver still has the technical ability to drive.
7n8v50.why: Revision can be ordered if there are doubts about the driver's technical ability (idoneità tecnica) to drive.

1aamiqk.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered with the obligation to undergo a medical examination and/or a technical aptitude test.
1aamiqk.why: Revision requires a medical examination and/or a driving aptitude test, depending on the doubts raised.

1m6md4y.q: Revision of the driving licence is ordered after the licence points have been reduced to zero.
1m6md4y.why: When all points are lost, the licence holder must take the revision exam (revisione).

1acifug.q: A driver who fails the licence revision exam has the licence revoked.
1acifug.why: Failing the revision exam means the licence is revoked (revoca).

ixoo8w.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder no longer meets the required moral requirements.
ixoo8w.why: Revision concerns physical, mental or technical fitness. Moral requirements are not a ground for it.

x82qd2.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder commits, twice in a year, an offence that results in the loss of at least 5 points.
x82qd2.why: Losing points, even repeatedly, does not trigger revision unless the points reach zero.

1tqqm07.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder permanently loses the required physical requirements.
1tqqm07.why: Permanent loss of physical requirements leads to revocation (revoca), not revision.

1hsg0nn.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder drives with the vehicle's roadworthiness inspection expired for more than a year.
1hsg0nn.why: An overdue vehicle inspection leads to a fine, not to a revision of the driving licence.

1xy8nk3.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder drives a historic car without the required documentation.
1xy8nk3.why: Missing documents for a historic car is only an administrative violation. It is not a ground for licence revision.

1kqtji7.q: Revision of the driving licence can be ordered when the holder drives a vehicle that is not theirs and has no written authorisation from the owner.
1kqtji7.why: Driving someone else's vehicle without written permission does not trigger a licence revision.

1e0bvgy.q: Revision of the driving licence is ordered when it is found that the driver is driving without having the licence with them.
1e0bvgy.why: Not carrying your licence results in a fine only. It does not lead to a revision.

1yuwl4w.q: A driver who fails the licence revision exam can repeat it two more times within a year, continuing to drive with a special permit issued by the Motorizzazione Civile.
1yuwl4w.why: Failing the revision exam leads to revocation. There is no special permit that allows you to keep driving and retake it.

btogtp.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the holder drives despite having a suspended licence.
btogtp.why: Driving while the licence is suspended results in revocation (revoca).

1njdpbq.q: Revocation of the licence can be ordered when the driver, on a motorway, reverses direction or drives the wrong way along the carriageway.
1njdpbq.why: Making a U-turn or driving against the traffic on a motorway can lead to revocation of the licence.

1ishurg.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the holder permanently loses the required physical requirements.
1ishurg.why: Permanent loss of physical fitness means the licence is revoked.

18t3zyj.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the holder permanently loses the required mental requirements.
18t3zyj.why: Permanent loss of the required mental fitness means the licence is revoked.

1sxrdc6.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when it is replaced by another licence issued by a foreign state.
1sxrdc6.why: When an Italian licence is converted into a foreign one, the Italian licence is revoked.

mw7t6v.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the holder, after undergoing the revision exam, is found no longer fit to drive.
mw7t6v.why: If the revision exam shows you are no longer fit to drive, the licence is revoked.

1k3tmsh.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the driver drives with a licence whose validity has expired.
1k3tmsh.why: Driving with an expired licence leads to a fine and withdrawal of the licence, not revocation.

v4joei.q: Revocation of the licence can be ordered when the driver drives without having it with them.
v4joei.why: Not carrying your licence results in a fine only, not revocation.

106uqs3.q: Revocation of the licence is ordered when the driver temporarily loses the physical requirements.
106uqs3.why: Only permanent loss of requirements causes revocation. A temporary loss does not.

9nbmwk.q: Revocation of the licence can be ordered when the driver drives without corrective lenses when they are required.
9nbmwk.why: Driving without prescribed corrective lenses brings a fine and suspension, not revocation.

12fwjpi.q: Revocation of the licence can be ordered by the police.
12fwjpi.why: Police cannot order revocation. It is ordered by the Prefect or the Motorizzazione civile.

18pete8.q: Revocation of the licence can be ordered when the driver drives a vehicle registered to another person without a written declaration.
18pete8.why: Driving a vehicle registered to someone else is legal and needs no written declaration, so it is no ground for revocation (revoca).

5ctrq3.q: Licence suspension is an accessory penalty arising from the violation of certain articles of the highway code.
5ctrq3.why: Suspension (sospensione) is an accessory administrative penalty attached to specific highway code violations, in addition to the fine.

1pnjq8d.q: Licence suspension is ordered, for example, when a newly licensed driver drives without respecting the restrictions on vehicles and speeds.
1pnjq8d.why: A new driver (neopatentato) who breaks the vehicle-power and speed restrictions that apply in the first years faces licence suspension.

1uxd0i8.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the maximum speed limits are exceeded by more than 40 km/h.
1uxd0i8.why: Exceeding the speed limit by more than 40 km/h brings licence suspension in addition to the fine.

1y3sobg.q: Licence suspension can be ordered when driving on the emergency lane of a motorway in cases not allowed by the highway code.
1y3sobg.why: Using the emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) on a motorway when not allowed leads to licence suspension, besides losing points.

cgi9k1.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver drives while under the influence of alcohol.
cgi9k1.why: Drink-driving leads to licence suspension, with a length that depends on the blood alcohol level.

ir152.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver refuses to undergo tests to check for possible alcohol intoxication.
ir152.why: Refusing alcohol tests is punished like the most serious level of drink-driving and brings licence suspension.

klx8vo.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver flees without helping the person who was hit.
klx8vo.why: Fleeing without helping a person you hit leads to licence suspension, besides criminal penalties.

1qwqq65.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver illegally drives a vehicle that has been seized.
1qwqq65.why: Driving a vehicle under seizure (sequestro) is a violation that carries licence suspension.

1tid5l6.q: Licence suspension can be ordered against someone who has forged or counterfeited the vehicle's insurance documents.
1tid5l6.why: Forging or counterfeiting a vehicle's insurance documents can result in licence suspension.

qwizqb.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the driver drives with a suspended licence.
qwizqb.why: Driving with a suspended licence leads to revocation (revoca) of the licence, not another suspension.

ty5u1h.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the licence holder permanently loses the physical requirements.
ty5u1h.why: Permanently losing the physical requirements leads to revocation (revoca), not suspension.

1t1uj2k.q: Licence suspension is ordered when doubts arise about whether the required fitness requirements still exist.
1t1uj2k.why: Doubts about the holder's continuing fitness lead to a licence revision (revisione), not suspension.

qrn0n4.q: Licence suspension is ordered together with the notification that the points have been reduced to zero.
qrn0n4.why: When points reach zero the licence must go through revision (revisione), with theory and practical tests, not suspension.

igtx4n.q: Licence suspension can be ordered when driving without having the driving licence with you.
igtx4n.why: Driving without the licence on you is punished only with a fine, not with suspension.

19xk1lg.q: Licence suspension is ordered when driving with an illegible or damaged licence.
19xk1lg.why: A damaged or illegible licence brings only a fine and the duty to replace it, not suspension.

rv5y53.q: Licence suspension is ordered when, at the request of the officers, you cannot show the warning triangle.
rv5y53.why: Failing to show the warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) is punished with a fine only, not licence suspension.

w6myer.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the holder no longer has the moral requirements.
w6myer.why: Losing the moral requirements leads to revocation (revoca) of the licence, not suspension.

hj9s1k.q: Licence suspension is ordered when a vehicle is left parked in spaces reserved for disabled people.
hj9s1k.why: Parking in disabled spaces brings a fine and lost points, but not licence suspension.

3ywirh.q: Licence suspension is ordered when the car's road tax (bollo) has not been paid on time.
3ywirh.why: Unpaid road tax (bollo) is a tax matter and does not lead to licence suspension.

1gbhgfn.q: Every driving licence has an initial allocation of 20 points.

yr3wm3.q: The licence points decrease when certain highway code violations are committed.
yr3wm3.why: Points are deducted only for specific violations that the highway code lists as carrying a points penalty.

1o1sq4h.q: When a driver has used up all the licence points, they must undergo a revision of the licence.
1o1sq4h.why: At zero points the licence must be revised (revisione), meaning new theory and practical tests.

j82s2x.q: Violations that cause point deductions, committed within the first three years of issue of a category B licence, are penalised with double the points.
j82s2x.why: In the first three years after getting a category B licence, the points deducted for each violation are doubled.

7iicq1.q: If several violations causing point loss are committed at the same time, at most 15 points can be deducted, unless they are violations leading to licence suspension.
7iicq1.why: For simultaneous violations the cap is 15 points, except for violations that carry licence suspension.

wmasyv.q: If a driver with fewer than 20 points commits no point-losing violations for two years, they regain all 20 points.
wmasyv.why: After two years without point-losing violations, a driver below 20 points is restored to 20.

74y7y2.q: Every driving licence has an initial allocation of 30 points.
74y7y2.why: The starting allocation is 20 points; 30 is only the maximum reachable through bonuses.

3oyd61.q: The licence points decrease when any highway code violation is committed.
3oyd61.why: Only certain listed violations cost points; many are punished with a fine alone.

gdtkyi.q: The licence points decrease only when a highway code violation is committed that carries suspension or withdrawal of the licence.
gdtkyi.why: Points are lost for many specific violations, even without suspension or withdrawal (ritiro), such as using a phone while driving.

1r375t0.q: Violations causing point deductions, committed within the first three years from the issue of the first licence, are penalised with triple the points.
1r375t0.why: In the first three years the points deducted are doubled, not tripled.

10ioeq.q: Attending a specific course and passing a specific exam allows the holder of an A or B licence to recover 9 points, up to a maximum of 30 points.
10ioeq.why: The recovery course with exam gives back 6 points for A and B licences, within the 30-point maximum.

s8g152.q: If several violations causing point loss are committed at the same time, at most 10 points can be deducted, unless they are violations leading to licence revocation.
s8g152.why: The cap for simultaneous violations is 15 points, and the exception covers violations leading to suspension, not revocation.

t3hfym.q: If a driver with fewer than 20 points commits no point-losing violations for two years, they get 30 points.
t3hfym.why: After two clean years, a driver below 20 points is restored to 20, not 30.

jf4v4h.q: When a driver has used up all the licence points, the licence is revoked.
jf4v4h.why: At zero points the licence is not revoked at once but must go through revision (revisione); revocation follows only if the exam is failed.

7h3vv8.q: Exceeding the speed limits by more than 10 km/h while driving causes a loss of points on the licence.
7h3vv8.why: Exceeding the limit by more than 10 km/h costs licence points, with more points lost the greater the excess.

pgya6r.q: Failing to respect some rules on overtaking causes a loss of points on the licence.
pgya6r.why: Breaking overtaking rules is among the violations that cost licence points.

1jcpmaw.q: Using a mobile phone without an earpiece or hands-free kit while driving causes a loss of points on the licence.
1jcpmaw.why: Holding a phone while driving brings a fine and loss of licence points.

sc02ah.q: Riding without a helmet when required, or with a badly fastened helmet, causes a loss of points on the licence.
sc02ah.why: A missing or badly fastened helmet, where required, brings a fine and loss of points.

11es4rk.q: Failing to keep the safety distance, resulting in an accident, causes a loss of points on the licence.
11es4rk.why: If failing to keep a safe distance causes an accident, points are lost in addition to the fine.

pop7en.q: Failing to use, or misusing, the lights while driving causes a loss of points on the licence.
pop7en.why: Not using lights, or using them improperly, is a violation that costs licence points.

vxqnda.q: Carrying an overload or too many passengers while driving causes a loss of points on the licence.
vxqnda.why: Overloading or carrying too many passengers brings a fine and loss of points.

4u1m06.q: Failing to wear lenses while driving, when prescribed, causes a loss of points on the licence.
4u1m06.why: Driving without the corrective lenses prescribed on the licence costs points.

1sjzq4x.q: Driving on the emergency lane of a motorway, outside the permitted cases, causes a loss of points on the licence.
1sjzq4x.why: Improper use of the motorway emergency lane (corsia di emergenza) brings a fine and loss of points.

1a5y4ws.q: Racing at speed on private tracks, being under 24 and holding only a B licence, causes a loss of points on the licence.
1a5y4ws.why: The ban concerns racing on public roads; on private tracks there is no violation, so no points are lost.

17wulh1.q: Leaving the car parked in front of a driveway entrance causes a loss of points on the licence.
17wulh1.why: Parking in front of a driveway (passo carrabile) is punished with a fine and towing, without point loss.

1xstgur.q: Driving without having the vehicle's registration document with you causes a loss of points on the licence.
1xstgur.why: Not carrying the registration document (carta di circolazione) brings a fine only, with no loss of points.

hlfx6x.q: Driving without having the vehicle's certificate of ownership with you causes a loss of points on the licence.
hlfx6x.why: The certificate of ownership does not have to be carried in the vehicle, so there is no penalty or point loss.

1wpgl13.q: Driving a vehicle owned by someone else without authorisation from the Motorizzazione Civile causes a loss of points on the licence.
1wpgl13.why: Driving someone else's vehicle is legal and needs no authorisation from the Motorizzazione, so no points are lost.

1uav880.q: The loss of licence points for a highway code violation is doubled if committed while riding a motorcycle with power over 35 kW.
1uav880.why: Doubled points apply to new drivers in their first three years, not according to the motorcycle's power.

1reejn0.q: The loss of licence points for a highway code violation is doubled if committed while driving a car with power over 115 kW.
1reejn0.why: Doubled points apply to new drivers in their first three years, not according to the car's power.

1upcmek.q: Driving a car with eight seats including the driver with a category C licence causes a loss of points on the licence.
1upcmek.why: A car with eight seats may also be driven with a category C licence, which covers larger vehicles; there is no violation or point loss.

n8o8sn.q: Driving a car on a motorway or main extra-urban road having held a category B licence for less than six months causes a loss of points on the licence.
n8o8sn.why: New drivers may use motorways; only the power and speed limits apply, so no points are lost for this.

1cs0hcn.q: Driving a loaded lorry with a gross weight under 3.5 tonnes on a public holiday causes a loss of points on the licence.
1cs0hcn.why: The holiday traffic ban applies to heavy vehicles over 7.5 t, not to lorries under 3.5 t, so no points are lost.

vfplur.q: Driving a vehicle that has not undergone the required periodic inspection causes a loss of points on the licence.
vfplur.why: A missing periodic inspection (revisione) brings a fine and withdrawal of the registration document, without point loss.

rj94n0.q: The driving licence is confirmed if its holder still has the required physical and mental requirements.
rj94n0.why: Renewal depends on the holder still meeting the required physical and mental fitness.

10niqp.q: The driving licence is confirmed following a favourable result of the medical check carried out by an authorised doctor.
10niqp.why: Renewal follows a favourable medical check by an authorised doctor.

1hb4zro.q: The driving licence is confirmed by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport following a psychophysical fitness check by an authorised doctor.
1hb4zro.why: The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport confirms the licence after the doctor's psychophysical fitness check.

1xw4g2d.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or renewed to someone not over 50.
1xw4g2d.why: A category B licence is valid for ten years up to age 50.

iuh6wj.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or renewed to someone aged between 50 and 70.
iuh6wj.why: Between ages 50 and 70 a category B licence is valid for five years.

1w3ode5.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for three years if issued or renewed to someone aged between 70 and 80.
1w3ode5.why: Between ages 70 and 80 a category B licence is valid for three years.

1l9skbm.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for two years if issued or renewed to someone over 80.
1l9skbm.why: Over age 80 a category B licence is valid for two years.

13riaua.q: Category BE licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or renewed to someone not over 50.
13riaua.why: Like category B, a BE licence is valid for ten years up to age 50.

2i862c.q: Category A licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years if issued or renewed to someone not over 50.
2i862c.why: A category A licence is also valid for ten years up to age 50.

wyw3py.q: Special category B (BS) licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or renewed to someone not over 70.
wyw3py.why: A special licence (BS) is valid for five years up to age 70.

zdh90s.q: The category B driving licence is confirmed by the Prefect following a check of the moral requirements.
zdh90s.why: Renewal requires a medical check of physical and mental fitness, not a moral-requirements check by the Prefect.

1un295a.q: With an expired driving licence it is still possible to keep driving for a maximum of three days.
1un295a.why: There is no grace period: you may not drive with an expired licence, or you face a fine and withdrawal of the licence.

fhl02.q: The driving licence is confirmed following a favourable result of a periodic practical driving test.
fhl02.why: Renewal is based on a medical examination, not on a periodic driving test.

1vpr2zv.q: The holder entitled to drive vehicles under category A and category B licences must, to confirm validity, undergo two specific medical examinations, each valid for one category.
1vpr2zv.why: A single medical examination renews all the categories the holder has.

1l95tq1.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for eight years if issued or renewed to someone aged between 50 and 70.
1l95tq1.why: Between ages 50 and 70 a category B licence is valid for five years, not eight.

1y3pv24.q: Category BE licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or renewed to someone not over 50.
1y3pv24.why: Up to age 50 a BE licence is valid for ten years, not five.

b2kcy8.q: The category B driving licence cannot be renewed for someone who has passed 80 years of age.
b2kcy8.why: Over 80 the category B licence can still be renewed, valid for two years, if fitness is confirmed.

pj2q9p.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for five years if issued or renewed to someone not over 50.
pj2q9p.why: Up to age 50 a category B licence is valid for ten years, not five.

1st8qi6.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document or aligned to the holder's birthday, is valid for ten years in every case of issue or renewal.
1st8qi6.why: Ten years applies only up to age 50; after that validity drops to 5, 3 and 2 years with age.

cr6b6j.q: Category B licence, unless otherwise restricted on the document, has no expiry until the holder turns 50.
cr6b6j.why: A category B licence always has an expiry date: ten years of validity up to age 50.
